utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good morning, Your Honours. This is IT-04-74-T, Prlic et al., the Prosecutor versus Prlic et al.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We -- we are the 28th of August. I'd like to greet all the people present in the courtroom, the representatives from the Prosecution, Defence counsel, as well as the accused. The cross-examination is about it to begin, and I shall ask the usher to go and fetch the witness. As far as time allocation is concerned, the Prosecution had just about three hours yesterday. The Defence teams will have is about three hours today, and it's for you to share out the time between you. I believe that Mr. Karnavas is going to start cross-examination because he has the lectern before him. Is that right, Mr. Karnavas? Mr. Ibrisimovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. IBRISIMOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Just for the record, in light of your proposal regarding the allocation of time, we will not be asking any questions and we will give our time to Mr. Prlic's Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning, Witness. We want to make sure that everything is unfolding properly, and I shall now give the floor to Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. President. Good morning, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Good morning, madam. Yesterday, you told us a little bit about your educational background. You had indicated that you had studied history, I believe; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, did you also studied journalism? Say yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I -- was one of my topics in the university was so-called communication science.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was that like a subject that you took, or was that part of a series of courses that you took?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I have even a university degree. I had six aims --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Stick with me on communications?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. Communications was one of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. So you took more than just one course?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you know university degrees, I have in my papers a degree from communication science.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And when you studied in Austria, was that communications or was that history?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was history.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now, yesterday you told us you were an historian as well?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you consider yourself an historian?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, but if I would have made my larger study, it would have been women in national socialist, in ideology and practice. So it has nothing to do with Balkans.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Very well. Now, and also you indicated that at one point that as part of your journalistic trait, you -- you do your own analysis.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because I have been studying history, politics, and economy, so I think that I can a little bit analyse.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you do know the difference between fact and, say, editorial opinion.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's say that an historian makes his opinions always on the facts.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But let me go back to my original question. You know the difference between fact: This happened today. We are in courtroom today, versus --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- your opinion as to your analysis of the events?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You know the difference?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the difference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, in fact, if you were to open up any credible paper, you have articles that are supposedly -- they're supposed to be factual, and then there's usually a portion of the paper that's devoted to editorial comment.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's a yes, right?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So you know the difference?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know the difference. And if I were to make an editorial comment, I could write for instance: On base of these facts, it could be like that. But, of course, there is other possibilities.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And, of course, when you are voicing your own opinion, it's necessary, it's appropriate to make sure that you make that distinction.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. In fact, that was the reason why I objected yesterday, as you might recall, because at one point it appeared that you were attributing certain comments, when in fact those were your own thoughts, your own opinions; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm, but based on certain facts, of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: When you say "Mm-hmm," does that mean yes?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We have to make a record. Okay? So now I want to go back to this interview. But before I go there, you had indicated that you had -- you were familiar about the Balkans, and in particular Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I was pretty familiar with the Balkans.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And I take it -- and you been to Bosnia and Herzegovina, I believe, in 1992?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, first time, I was 1968.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But I'm not asking about the first time. I'm talking about 1992. My questions are rather precise.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay, okay. I was 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I take it you followed the Vance-Owen peace initiatives? It is a "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I followed them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, does that mean -- we're going to go step-by-step. I'll lead you through it. Does that mean that you were in Geneva covering them, or does that mean that you were reading the press?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was reading only the press, but the leader of Bosnia-Herzegovina group was the Finn Martti Ahtisarri.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So what does that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It means that it had, of course, a little bit more interesting Finland than when it had been somebody else.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was he one of the prime negotiators with Vance, with Mr. Vance?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He was the senior [indiscernible] peaceable group, or how you call it?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was six different sections, and Ahtisarri was the president of Bosnia-Herzegovina group.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, are you suggesting, though, that it was he, along with Mr. Vance and Mr. Owen, that were meeting with the various parties to try and to piece together a peace agreement?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you interview him personally regarding --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ahtisarri, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you interview Mr. Vance?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you interview Mr. Owen?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And you -- you were not in Geneva at the time?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what you know about the Vance-Owen is about what you read in the press?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the treaty somewhere because the press could get also the treaty.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to get there. Now, did you -- do you recall reading the treaty at the time? And it was a peace initiative; it wasn't a treaty.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. It was an initiative.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you read it?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I read did but -- but not by heart.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when -- not by heart. Okay. Now, before we get there, I got to step back a little bit. Now, prior to the Vance-Owen peace initiatives, were there any other initiatives? You being an historian covering the events, being a journalist, were there any other initiatives that you recall, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Which one were those?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Vance-Stoltenberg.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Let me clue you in. That happened afterwards.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was afterwards, but it was the correction from Vance-Owen.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But I'm talking about before Vance-Owen. Do you know, do you know, okay? I don't want you to speculate. Do you know for a fact, yes, there were, or maybe at the time I might have known. What is your answer?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There was.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And which were -- which initiatives were there, if you recollect?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember but I know that there was other negotiations and other initiatives.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, was that again based on reading the press?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Does that mean that you actually read those initiatives?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, I reading the press or visit the --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you read the initiatives, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not totally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well what do you mean "not totally"? Did you read them partially?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That means you had a hold of them. You had them in your possession?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. But you can also -- I visit so-called press bureaus.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So, again, you were reading the press?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If I read papers in some press bureau, it's not reading the press.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So what were you actually reading at the press bureau and which press bureaus were you reading at and which initiatives were you reading at these press bureaus, if you recollect?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, after 15 years to remember in -- in which bureaus you have once visited, it's not that easy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Which initiatives and who are the protagonists? Who were like, for instance, the negotiators? Which countries? Names?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, the country, it was also a little bit problematic because -- because Bosnia-Herzegovina, Croatia, and so on, they were not all the time recognised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, if I tell you something about, for instance, beginning of 1992, so there was 15th of January, Slovenia and Croatia was recognised but Bosnia, first, after the war had started in April. So -- there's a pretty big difference, but I know that there was one very important initiative before Vance-Owen, I know it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, you know it. Do you know the specifics, and by that I mean: Can you give us a comparison? Can you compare and contrast the difference between the initiative prior to Vance-Owen and what ultimately emerged from Vance-Owen? And I mention this particularly because, yesterday, you mentioned -- you gave your own interpretation as to the Vance-Owen Plan and what it attempted to accomplish or what it was.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, you know, that there was also --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you could answer my question.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- a big peace conference in London. It was August 1992, and there was also some initiatives. But I would say that Vance-Owen was the first one which was very official and which the whole international community was backing.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, Mr. Vance, as you well know, was with the United Nations at the time; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And Mr. Owen was the representative for the European Union or the European Community, I think it was at the time it.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Now -- and yesterday you indicated that that -- you said something about -- maybe it's because of your English --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not very good any more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I mean it's not bad. Better than my Finnish. But I wasn't quite -- I didn't quite get the drift of what you were trying to tell us when you said that you compared it to, you said, the 1938 --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I was correcting the 1939 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. To the Sporazum. And I am trying to figure out what you were trying to tell us about that. Could you expand a little bit? How is it --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only, only --.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You need to wait until I completely entire question because part of the question is: How is it that you now are attributing Mr. Vance and Mr. Owen of trying to create something similar to the 1939 Sporazum?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, Mr. -- The Vance and Owen plan had a map.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And this map, if you take this had -- well, that what was promised for Croatians or the mixed cantons or how they were called. The boundary line was very equal to this from Sporazum 1939.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only that the population was not any more exactly that what it was been 1939. It has changed. It was more Bosniaks. There were 1939, I think, with Croat majority, but not any more 1992. And that was what I was criticising because there was some kind of similarity. But -- and as I told you also that it was told to me, for instance from Lagumdzija, that it was not meant ethnical, but it was interpreted ethnical, and maybe exactly because of these similarities of Sporazum.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But, fair to say, you actually did not look at the Vance-Owen peace initiatives, and there was more than just one by the way.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes. There were more.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah. And we'll get to that. But you did not study them to see and compare what exactly was in the text and what exactly was on the maps; is that correct? It's just a yes or a no.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not totally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, when you say "not totally," did you -- did you study them partially?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of course. I wouldn't speak about Vance-Owen Plan --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- if I never saw it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So, today, you're saying, under oath, that you read the Vance-Owen Plan from A to Z, whichever plan might have been, and you looked at the maps as well?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Especially the maps --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may, just for the purpose of the record, if we look at line -- at page 11, line 7, there's stands: "I never saw it." And I think because of the overlapping speakers, I recall the witness said: "I wouldn't speak about the Vance-Owen Plan if I never saw it." It does make a difference. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's fine. We're going to get to this. We're going to unpeel this onion.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, I want to know concretely: Did you read the Vance-Owen peace initiatives?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but I don't remember them.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: From the beginning to the end, you read them?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Like journalists read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I don't know how -- I haven't --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't read them in that meaning like I'm --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Like an analyst or an historian.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- you are comparing me to do something. I just read them, because I never commented them in that way.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE PRANDLER
utterances.text: May I interrupt you. Both of you please do not overlap.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I apologise. I apologise. I'm trying to save time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Here is where I am a little troubled. Yesterday, you told us that you were an analyst, that you were in an historian. In fact, you were kind of insistent, and I kept getting these guarded looks for you. I felt rather hurt, actually, when I was objecting, and you were looking at me sort of like as if I was challenging your integrity. And now, today, you're telling us, as a journalist -- albeit you were asking questions regarding the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, and you were commenting yesterday about the Vance-Owen Peace Plan and what the Croats had in mind. Today you're telling us that you read it like a journalist, whatever that means. But then you go on to say that you really didn't read them carefully to prepare yourself for interviews. So could you clarify this? Help me out here.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, prepare yourself for interviews. How I prepare me -- me to interview, when I have about five minutes time even to know whom I'm going to interview, if you ask somewhere where is happening very much, you have to make interviews spontaneously. You cannot prepare weeks. If I know that I have next week the interview of president of Croatia, Stipe Mesic, I should prepare me. But if I know that I meet Stipe Mesic, after five minutes there, I just think what I'm going to ask him, but I cannot prepare with reading treaties or something like that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Fair enough. Before we get to this interview, you were the one that went to Mostar; right? You weren't summoned?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was in Mostar.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But you went there on your own initiative?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You picked the date? You picked the day, the month, the year, the date?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: April.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yeah. But you picked the day?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You picked that location?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You went there on your own initiative searching for a story?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You had heard some things prior to going to the -- to Mostar; right?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And because of what you had heard, you wanted to get more information.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wanted to see what has happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You weren't interested in information, you just wanted to see, take a look, was that it?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, both. You have to see and you have to ask --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One step at a time. The first thing that you do is you go to the press officer; right?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes -- no, no. That was not the first time. It was the second. I told you that we were first driving around and looking.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You drove around, you look, and then you went to the press office, hoping, hoping that there would be somebody that you could speak with?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And then you -- you got an interview.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: One would assume, one would assume, that since you chose to go to Mostar on that particular day, at that particular location, that you would have some thoughts in mind as to what exactly you were going to ask about. Is it a "yes," "no," "it doesn't work that way"?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it doesn't work that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. I'm not a journalist. Help me out here. How does it work?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it works that way because when I went, when I started the trip in Mostar, I was not informed what had happened in Central Bosnia. I was not informed because I was not there. There was coming very specially anything, and maybe there was some knowledge of what had happened in -- in Bosnia. Maybe there was. But I was in Croatia and Croatian media didn't tell about these things, and I was listening BBC. But in BBC, there was also nothing to hear. It means that I didn't know. I was much wiser first in the evening of that day.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But, nonetheless, before you got there, you knew about the Vance-Owen Peace Plan?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes, I knew.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. At least, with respect to that, you were prepared to ask some questions?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not necessarily.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, yesterday, there was a whole exchange, ad nauseam actually, over and over, because we went back and forth about this ultimatum. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And the ultimatum, at least the way they try weave it in - "they" being the Prosecution - was based on the Vance-Owen Peace Plan; right?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It based because it was some cantons which was demanded that Muslim forces retreat, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And it's your understanding that these -- that these cantons, if you look at the map and you look at the cantons that were in dispute, we would see a map similar to the 1939 Sporazum; is that your understanding?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Let's get to the interview very quickly, because we have to move along. At some -- you asked the press officer to meet someone, and you learned that you were going to be meeting with Jadranko Prlic?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's a yes, right?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, before meeting Mr. Prlic, I take it you had, since this is 1993 now, you had been in country in 1992. You had been following the situation in Bosnia-Herzegovina. I take it that you had a clear understanding and appreciation of how Herceg-Bosna was structured and how the HVO, the Croatian Community of Herceg-Bosna, was structured, politically and militarily?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know about political structure. I knew the military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Did you ask anybody, prior to being to Mostar, what the political structure was? "Yes," "no," "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Did you ask anybody when you got to Mostar about it? Say "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. The reason I'm asking is because, yesterday, you indicated that Mr. Prlic was the head of the military.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Political head of military.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Political head of the military. Okay. And did you ask him to explain his position?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, no. Just say "yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Pardon?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You can read what?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: His card.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So, based on his card, you made certain assumptions.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, "president" is a political leader, normally.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And it was your -- and it was your assumption that "HVO" meant the military.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Fair enough. But you never asked him: What exactly does your title entail? What are your functions?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The leader of HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. And then, yesterday, you sort of likened him to into a defence minister.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I would compare him to a defence minister.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So, in your mind, in your mind, when you were speaking with Jadranko Prlic, you were, for all intents and purposes, speaking with a defence minister?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, something similar to defence minister. You know, in former Yugoslavia, minister is used to be committees and so on. You can title it very many different ways.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. Okay. All right. And, in your statement, you say at some point you go to a presidential villa, and it's in quotes, "presidential villa." Do you recall saying that in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You've said it?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have said it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, when you said "presidential villa" in the quotes, does that mean that you saw a sign saying "Presidential Villa"?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That's why it is --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: In quotes?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I see. Usually, when people quote, it's because that's what somebody actually said?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it's -- it is another way. You use this in two meanings. In that, when you are saying something uncertain, which is not directly or then accurate quotation, but that was not quotation. It was so-called.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So meaning so-called.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. All right. And you say, in your statement, that you suspect that the HVO was very eager to -- to tell the story to the international press at this time.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: You say that on page 5 of your -- now, I take it you were the one that went there; right? He didn't summon you.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, let's say that a press officer organised it very quickly, and it looked like -- because normally it was not that easy to become an interview. And I would --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- Tell you something. I'm not an important person. I'm from Finland. It's a very remote country. It has no political meaning to Herceg-Bosna, but I was working also for Austria press agency, which is much more important. And I was with Erich Rathfelder who was working for Germany and Swiss. So we were only two persons but we had very much press behind us, and that's why I think we were so, well, invited to this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. But you drew a conclusion, I suspect, that had Mr. Prlic refused to meet with you or anybody else, then you probably would have said in your statement that they were not eager to tell their story. You would draw the opposite conclusion; right? So they're sort of dammed if they do and they are dammed if they don't. If they speak with you, then obviously they're eager to get their message out. If they do not speak with you, they're not eager. Would that be correct?

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I may object to this question. The witness never said that she asked to see Mr. Prlic. So now to suppose that if Mr. Prlic had refused to see her is an improper question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If the gentleman to read the rest of the question, the rest of the question, or anybody else, that the press officer refused.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you had been denied access to anybody on that occasion, as you indicated that you sat many times outside the door of Mate Boban but it never opened, would you have written that they were probably not very eager to tell their story?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't have written it because it would have been a normal -- a normal case.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, on page 1 of the transcript of the interview --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I don't have it here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. We're going to get you a copy.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, I'm going to be referring to 1D 01655 for the record. Yesterday, last night, we listened to the tape. We listened to it about three times, and we found that there was some discrepancies, some omissions. For instance, on side B, we couldn't hear anything, even though there is some -- some things attributed to as to what might have been said during the interview; and on side A, there seem to be some omissions. And, obviously, I think, because of the poor quality of the tape, you have to sort of listen to it over and over again. But we would be asking at some point -- we don't want to take up the Court's time to play it here. But we tried our best, and at some time we will probably need to send this out and maybe get a cleaner and even a more official version. So just so you know, Your Honours, and everyone else in the court, the portions where we believe the words or sentences were missing, we have put in in bold and we've underlined. That way you can easily track. And because we have to insert text, the pagination is slightly different from the original version that was presented by the Prosecution. The number is 1D 01655. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you have it ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, again, you know, we have the tape and that could be checked.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, in the very first -- after he welcomes you, I think it's the second paragraph, Mr. Prlic says: "You will hear it at the conference at 1100 hours," or 11 hours.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. Prlic was holding a press conference that day, was he not?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because I was not in that press conference. We started immediately after interview to go to Central Bosnia because we were thinking that in the press conference, there is not much more what we have been talking with him. I was not in this press conference.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But you were made aware that there was a press conference on that particular day?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, according to Mr. Prlic, there was. I don't know because we didn't attend it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, did you find out later on what he might have said at that press conference?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Okay. Now, during the interview, you asked him several -- you asked him at one point -- you asked him about the ultimatum. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- I ask him about it. I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. And, if we go on the second page of your interview, you ask him, at the very top of the page, first -- first question by you: "Why then talk about a common command and Mr. Izetbegovic" and so on and so forth. Now, what was your understanding of "a common command"?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: My understanding about "common command" was that Bosnian army and HVO would have common command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That was part of the Vance-Owen Peace Plan, was it not? Part of the initiative?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Was it part of the initiative, ma'am? "Yes," "no," "I don't know." Which of those?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but it was very much talked at that time.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Because you asked the question, so you must have heard it somewhere?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Oh, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, in fact, prior to this interview, you had met with Mr. Hadzihasanovic, the general?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I met with Hadzihasanovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And had he talked about the initiative as far as a common command?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know whether a common command was signed, agreed upon, a joint command?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was maybe signed but it was not realised.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know when it was signed?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you recall the reasons for wanting a joint command?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And what were the reasons, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To defend Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Exactly. Now, also does not Mr. Prlic say that -- that: "There is no possibilities to be successful in war if you have two armies in the same region." He says that, does he not?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And that's exactly the reason for common command.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Right. And he's trying to explain to you the reasons why in some places the HVO wanted the ABiH to be subordinated to the HVO and vice versa. In other areas, the HVO would be subordinated to the ABiH. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but that story.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: That's what he's telling you, is he not?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm. That's what he's telling.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, and, in fact, the Joint Command, that is one the reasons for having a Joint Command; right?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Were you aware that on -- on 25th of April, 1993, that would be one day after this interview, in fact, President Izetbegovic and Mate Boban signed a joint statement ordering a cease-fire between the ABiH and HVO units and setting up a Joint Command? Were you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, later, but not in Central Bosnia, because I was, at that time, in Central Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. But you were aware that, in fact, that did happen. In fact, I'm reading from page 631 of the -- of the final judgement, trial judgement in Hadzihasanovic. So you were aware of that? So exactly what Mr. Prlic is telling you is in fact what's happening.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but you have to make some difference between theory and practice. In practice, there was a war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand that there was a war, and both sides were -- were fighting against each other; right?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mm-hmm.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: "Mm-hmm," does that mean yes?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, there were many wars at that time. There was the first war against Serbs, and that was the so-called second Bosnian war. It was the Bosniaks and Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And there was also a third kind of situation in Tuzla, in Gradac. That's where I was interviewing somebody from MHVO, Muslim HVO, in the same when the Muslims were kicked out. In Herceg-Bosna, they were fighting together in -- in Posavina. It was not that simple, that situation.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, they were fighting together also in Sarajevo, were they not? Was not an HVO --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Sarajevo, they were also fighting together, but there was the Muslim part much stronger. But in Posavina, there were also very many Croats.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, in Sarajevo, in fact, the HVO was subordinated to the ABiH.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At what time?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At this time.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Maybe. I was not at this time in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well. Now, if we go on to the interview - because I'm just going to take your interview first, and then we'll go through some of your statements - you say, in the middle of page 2 --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: This is something that was injected, Your Honour, by us last night, and we see -- you will see that we have the timing as far as where it's on the tape itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: "When I remember right, in January 24, Mr. Rajic ordered or was it you ordered to take over Gornji Vakuf?" And then you go on: "To control Gornji Vakuf by HVO in our information are that you moved artillery from Tomislavgrad area into this area at Gornji Vakuf. This was in January. So first strike was sent by you." So this is your statement to Mr. Prlic. Now, where did you get this information that it was the HVO that had the first strike, if you recall?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: BritBat.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, he goes on to say: "No. You know, any truth is just one truth. You have information only from one side." And then he talks about fortification, and then he lists several places where he's saying: "There are no possibilities to achieve Novi Travnik, Travnik, Busovaca, and any other place in middle Bosnia and in Northern Bosnia," and he goes on and on. Were you aware of any of these events, concretely?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: These events which occurred in Central Bosnia, I was aware of them after this interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. So you were -- after this I view, you became aware that Muslims were attacking Croats in Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I didn't became aware of that. I became aware that Croats were attacking Muslims in central Croatia. I went in the same day to Ahmici, and I saw the burning villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Let me ask you --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: So that's why I'm telling that this is not quite truth.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, madam, when you went to Central Bosnia, at that particular time, did you at any point learn that Muslims had also been attacking Croatian villages? "Yes" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That time -- well, there came -- when we were waiting to get to Ahmici, there came two women to our car for the British --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: No, ma'am. Ma'am --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- press conference, and they were claiming that their village was attacked, but I personally saw only burning Muslim villages.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So when these two women told you about that, did you go to verify as a good journalist, historian, analyst?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I go to Ahmici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was waiting to go there.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. So you didn't verify any of that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't go after the story of these two women.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well, did you learn, at that point, that the Muslims had also been attacking Croat villages?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I learned it and it was really true, but, first, much later in Kraljevska Sutjeska area. But it was much, much later. Yes. I saw destroyed villages there, but it was one year later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You saw them one year later.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: But not these villages. They were other ones: Vares area and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. I'm going to move ahead a little bit, just to make a point here. You indicated, at one point, that you had met -- I believe it's in your statement that you had met - if I can find it here real quickly - Mr. Mehmed Alagic; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. You met him in Central Bosnia in 1993?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I met Alagic -- Mehmed Alagic, and also Zuskic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And they were the commandants of Travnik.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: We're going to go step-by-step. Now, according to your statement --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: It's page 7, last paragraph, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And I'm referring to exhibit -- it's your statement. I don't have the exhibit number handy, but I will get it for you in a second. But it's on page 7. You say: "While in Central Bosnia, in April 1993, I also met with Bosnian Muslim leaders," and then you go on: "Mehmed Alagic gave me a declaration of observance of standards in the conduct of war, which he told me all his soldiers were to sign," and then you gave that copy to the ICTY. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And then you claimed -- then you go on to say: "Moreover, Alagic claimed that all sides in the war only the ABiH soldiers were behaving." Right?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, first of all, this would have been in April, so that would have been before you met with Mr. Prlic or after?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was after.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm just asking. One step at a time. Okay. Now, did you by any chance read that declaration? Did you read the declaration, ma'am, the one that you handed to the ICTY, the one that Mr. Alagic gave you with respect to the standards that his soldiers were to -- to abide by? It's a "yes"" or "no."

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can read it, but I don't understand that well this language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let me ask you this: Yesterday, you indicated that you could read Croatian, and I understand that we have -- we call it here B/C/S. And that's a whole big dispute about the languages?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Serbian, Croatian. Was this -- was this language any different than the one that you were reading in the press that you claimed that you were able to follow the story line in the press?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I can follow the story line because press language is little bit easier, but official documents I'm not able to -- to read that well. And when I'm reading press, I used also dictionary to know. Press language is easier.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Fair enough. Now, when you met with Mr. Alagic, did you have an interpreter, a translator, with you?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: A language assistant?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I suspect that language assistant would have been able to have -- to read this document.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I suppose so.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, the answer is: Yes, they would have been able to; right?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, he would have been able to.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. There you go. Now, did you ask your language assistant to read you the document to see what exactly he had handed you?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because I didn't think it very important at that moment. Which newspaper would have been publishing for me that kind of document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm not saying whether it was, you know, necessary to publish it but just to read it since you're testifying here today.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: And, Your Honours, for the record, this document is -- is 1D 01653. We're just going to look at that time very quickly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If you look at the very top of, it says: "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, Code of fighters for Bosanska Krajina." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Do you know where Bosanska Krajina is, ma'am?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know. But I know also that the --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the speakers please not overlap.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- that the troop of Alagic was so-called Krajina Brigade, because it was consisted from the refugees from Bosanska Krajina. It means from Northern Bosnia. That's why it was using this name.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. I -- I know, but it wasn't a tricky question. If we go down -- if we go to the first bullet, it says: "Bosnian Herzegovina is an independent, sovereign, integral, and indivisible state." Do you know what they mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose that -- that they are thinking Bosanska Krajina, because they were refugees with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because it was under Serbian control.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Could they also be thinking unitary, that this is a way of promoting the concept of a unitary form of government in Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And by "unitary," do you know what -- what we mean by that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I mean that all three nations are sharing part in the government and not making their own small states.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Well "unitary," ma'am, at the time, was meant that it would be one person, one vote. And so if you were -- had, say, as the Muslims did at the time, you had the largest percentage of population, if it would be one person one vote and that's how the power sharing would be, then other national constituent nations would have less power. Did you know that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, and I never learned that kind of things.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Very well.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Because --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- because you don't have to have the same person to have share of power.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Okay. Very well. We go on. On bullet 3, it says: "Personnel and joint weapons, as well as other material and technical resource," and then it says: "Armed combat is a holy thing and a final victory and a free Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina." Now, what do they mean by "combat is a holy thing"? Keeping in mind that we're talking about a -- fighters that are Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: Mr. Karnavas, aren't you asking the witness to speculate?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm asking whether she knows. She can certainly say: "I don't know." And there is a purpose for this, Your Honour, and the purpose is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I don't doubt that. I don't doubt that there is a purpose to your questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. But she can say: "I don't know."

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Do you know?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No what?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: What they mean by this: "Armed combat is a holy thing"?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think they mean just nothing. It's such a beautiful sentence in --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And, of course, had you had it translated at the time, you might have been able to get Mr. Alagic to explain exactly what he meant, since he had told you that he was insisting on all his soldiers signing this document. Part of the point I'm trying to make. You never ask him though --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- to explain this? Okay. Now, if we go further down, it says at one point: "I shall treat the prisoners and civilian in the spirit of orders and in line with the Geneva Convention." You see that? It's one, two, three, four, five, six seven. It's the seventh bullet point, after it, it says: "before, during, and after combat operations."

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On the same document that we are --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this -- this Bosnian document?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. You see that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All right. Well, it's there. It's on the seventh bullet point. But, in any event, after meeting with Mr. Alagic, you were left with the impression that they were abiding or his people, his soldiers were abiding by the standards and conduct of war; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. And I was also talking about this thing with the BritBat, because, you know, in Vitez there was a BritBat. And the British press officer told me that it was a very disciplined, elite troop.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Now, if we could look at just very briefly -- if we could look at 1D 01654. This is the indictment from the Office of the Prosecution. It's an amended indictment. It's dated 11th January 2002, so it comes from them. I didn't draft it; they did. And you will see that Mr. Mehmed Alagic, who is no longer with us, was indicted at the time. Do you see that? It's the very top of the page. The Prosecution --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The first page.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes. You see that? Now, if we go to the fourth page, four page of 16, you will see it. We have numbered paragraphs, and it says on 19, for instance: "Non-Bosnian citizens. In August 1st, 1992, a law on service of ABiH was introduced via presidential decree. Under the law, non-Bosnian citizens were allowed to join the ABiH and be promoted during times of war." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Were you aware, at the time, that Mr. Alagic had in his -- under him, foreign fighters.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Those were the Mujahedin, were they not?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Not only. But he had Mujahedin under him, "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was driving these villages which were told there are Mujahedin, and I saw 12. The Brits were telling there were about 150.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, you learned this when? In April 1993 or later?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Later.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was also later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, this was signed in 1992. Did Mr. Alagic, by an chance, share with you that information that he had foreign fighters, including fighters who had been rather seasoned as a result of their combat experience in fighting the Soviet Union in Afghanistan?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, I want to correct myself. I found that there are foreign Mujahedins, first, one year or two years later, because I met a Finnish one who was fighting under Alagic.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't know at that stage, but I am aware because I learned it later.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, if we go down, it says later on, on page -- I'm going to skip --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, my attention is being drawn to time. Mr. Ibrisimovic was saying that he gave you the time that he had at his disposal, but that means that your time plus his is still running out at this time. I think that some of the other Defence counsels may have given you their time, possibly Mr. Coric's counsel who just rose, is that right, and Mr. Murphy as well? Yes. Well, that's fine. All their time. This means that after you only Mr. Praljak will be left; is that right? So, for the cross-examination, there will only be Mr. Praljak after you, and the Defence of Petkovic, unless Petkovic Defence has also given you their time? Ms. Alaburic?

utterances.speaker: MS. ALABURIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, we intend to cross-examine this witness. However, if Mr. Karnavas needs some time, we'll come to some arrangement in the meantime.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. And for Praljak, the position is?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOVACIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Praljak could perhaps give five or ten minutes of his time. He was thinking along those lines, but he hasn't decided yet.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Sorry, Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: For the record, we do have tomorrow that's vacant.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: But if we could go on to this indictment --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand, I understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not tomorrow. Not tomorrow. Mr. Karnavas, tomorrow there is no hearing. You're say tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I understand. Your Honour, the record I'm trying to make is that we are restricting the Defence from putting on their case with vital and important witnesses, even when there's free days available to the parties. That's all I'm trying to say, Your Honour. It can be interpreted however one wishes to interpret that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: On paragraph --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, I can't allow that. I told you last week that administration has placed us before the fact of having cancelled Wednesday's hearing, and I explained to you that there was seven trials underway requiring three courtrooms. The administration has decided to cancel some days of certain trials. That's what happened. That is the reason why we do not have a hearing tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I misunderstood. I thought that perhaps the Prosecution ran out of witnesses and that's why.

utterances.speaker: MR. STRINGER
utterances.text: Just for the record, Mr. President, the Prosecution did to the run out of witnesses, and it was our understanding that we were not having court tomorrow because of scheduling of other cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: All I know is this: We've been in a race. We've been in a race with a stopwatch approach, and all I know is that my client is looking at many, many years in prison. And I've said it before, I'll it, and I'll keep saying it: In my opinion, when we have important witnesses, such as this witness, having a strict compliance to some arbitrary time constraint is not a way to properly afford these gentlemen, particularly my client, his due process. But be that, as it may, I would just like to continue --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Mr. Karnavas. I would like you to correct and control your language.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You speak of arbitrary time restraints. There is no reason why you speak of arbitrary time restraints. You have know that there have been several complaints. The Appeals Chamber has always upheld this Trial Chamber's restrictions on time. You know what you complained about regarding tomorrow was a clear mistake, which you could have avoided if you had been attentive, because the President has drawn attention to this. So do not accuse anybody of arbitrariness if you have no foundation for it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: The foundation, Your Honour, is - and this has been a constant complaint - those of us who have practised law in courtrooms, those of us who are seasoned lawyers know that you don't simply add one and one and come up with two when it comes to trial. You don't say: The Prosecution took three hours, therefore, six accused will divide three hours among themselves. That is not a way to run an efficient trial. That's not a way to protect the rights of the accused. The world over, there are two basic concepts: One, is it relevant, and two, is it non-repetitive. In this instance, we have a very vital witness. Now, we had Mr. Okun here, an ambassador who spent two years with two thousand pages of documents. I was not allowed to get the documents in; I ran out of time. Now, that is -- if that is not arbitrary, if that's not capricious, I don't know what is. That's my interpretation. Now, the Appeals Chamber can say what it wishes with respect to the Trial Chamber imposing these sorts of restrictions; but if we look at witness per witness, there are times when we need to go beyond the three-hour limit or the five-hour limit, however the Prosecution's time is. It's simply impossible for the Defence to cover everything. I sat here yesterday, and this witness spoke almost exclusively about Mr. Prlic. There are six other accused. They're all entitled to their time. If another accused wanted to use up their time, I would have been left for 30 minutes. If you're telling me that that's fair allocation and that's justice, I must say, Your Honour, that is not true, that's not correct, and I would protest to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE TRECHSEL
utterances.text: You always have ample time for complaining, Mr. Karnavas. You could spare some of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: I'm merely making my record, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: If we go to paragraph 22 of the indictment, you will see there that they talk about that in November 9, 1992, the ABiH chief of the General Staff issued an order, specific types of units of the ABiH corps, 3rd Corps, allowing for various TO units and headquarters to merge. You see that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. And, of course, if we go -- if we go further up to paragraph 20, we see that there is the establishment of the ABiH corps. You see that?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, at the time that you gave your -- you had your interview with Mr. Prlic, you had indicated at one point that it was your understanding that the ABiH was merely a Territorial Defence?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It based on the Territorial Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you were claiming that that's what it was, that it was a Territorial Defence, and he had -- he corrected you and said that, you know, they have corps. And you cannot have a Territorial Defence based on a corps, or you can't have is corps based on Territorial Defence; correct?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, we have -- we have maybe a language problem. I mean that Bosnian army was builded on the basic of Territorial Defence, because JNA, you know, it was the Yugoslavian army, and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. If we can skip on because I'm running out of time here. Paragraph 23, we see there's a reference to the 7th Mountain Brigade. But on paragraph 24, we see -- and I'll just read it for the record: "The ABiH 3rd Corps 7th Mountain -- Muslim Mountain Brigade was an all-Muslim unit. Soldiers within this unit were required to strictly adhere to Islamic beliefs. Recruits had to swear an oath, which included that they would follow the example of a prophet -- of a proper Muslim soldiers as set out in the booklet titled: Instructions to the Muslim Fighter. The Instructions on the Muslim Fighter was initially published in 1993."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ANTONETTI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Karnavas, the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KRUGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I'm sorry to interrupt. But Your Honour, especially in light of the time constraints of Mr. Karnavas, I have difficulty in seeing the relevance of the question -- of this line of questioning. I have to object to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, I'm glad that he objected to this unrelevance The relevance is this: It goes to bias. She meets with Mr. Alagic in 1993 in April. She claimed yesterday, she's claiming today that nothing was happening to the Croats because part of the interview, if you keep in mind, this is now 24th of April. The events in Ahmici happened on the 16th. The Prosecution would want everybody to believe that as a result of this ultimatum, the passage of time then unleashed all of these events in Central Bosnia and, therefore, that is part of the joint criminal enterprise and something that we need to defend against. Okay. That's their theory. Fine. They're entitled to it. She wants to back it up. And if we keep going, because I'm not through with this, we will see, at least on -- when we get to the counts, the charges, for instance, on paragraph 40, we talk -- they talk about certain events that happened, lo and behold, in April 1993. But before we get there, because this gentlewoman seems to think that Mr. Alagic with his altruistic expressions, that only the ABiH soldiers were complying and hands out, and hands out this little pamphlet, it turns out that even the Prosecution admit that, in fact, they were handing out the instructions of the Muslim fighters, which we saw through Witness Smajkic. And if you see in the indictment, they talk about what to do with war prisoners, including exterminating them. And the question is: If this is not on -- why wasn't Mr. Alagic questioned about this? Was she aware of this? Then, when we go to paragraph 40, and I quote: "Between January 1993 and January 1994, the ABiH was engaged in combat activities with the HVO in Central Bosnia. In particular, in April 1993 and in early summer 1993, ABiH 3rd Corps units launched a series of heavy attacks against the HVO including, but not limited, to the areas of the municipalities of Bugojno, Busovaca, Kakanj, Maglaj," and so on and so forth. Some of these areas, Your Honours, were the topic of the conversations that this woman was having -- this witness was having with Mr. Prlic during the interview. So I'm -- she's supposed to be a journalist. She said she was an historian. One would expect, especially, Mr. President, based on your question to her, that she would have done some preparation prior to, because she's forming an opinion and writing an article thereafter, basically saying the Croats are lying. The Croats are sugar coating. And it is only the Croats who are committing these atrocities with the Muslims being the victims, and that the Croats are playing it vice versa. And what I'm trying to show is that this interview is incomplete. It doesn't tell the entire story. It's not in perspective, and this woman -- this witness is not credible. Not that she's necessarily biased, but she doesn't have all the facts at the time. That's the whole purpose, and I hope it answers the gentleman's question.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Now, madam, were you aware that the ABiH was handing out these instructions, called Instructions for Muslim Fighter, where it was talking about jihad and talking about what to do with prisoners, war booty, and so on, just as -- and this is 1D 00505, for the record. Were you aware of that? And this was coming out of Zenica, by the way. Were you aware of that, "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that moment, no.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: At which moment did you become aware of it --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- and where is it in your statement?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, it has nothing to do with this, but, let's say, it is very much propaganda about Mujahedin and so on. But there were not that many. As the Brits thought, there were about 150. And about --

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Excuse me, ma'am --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- about these sections, I heard from a Finnish man who was fighting in Muslim Corps, and he was telling that there were some radicals, but the most of them were laughing at it. And I must tell you that the Finnish man was certainly no Muslim, but it was first after, when I met him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well, there have been figures as much as high as 7.000 --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: -- of foreign fighters?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It has been. But, anyway, these Brits were counting villages behind Travnik, and they found 150. I found 12.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: So, in other words, the Prosecution, in drafting this indictment, after what it did, you know, in preparing the indictment, investigating, what have you, were actually hoodwinked. They didn't know what they were doing?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say that. I told only what I heard from BritBat and what I saw myself, because I cannot witness things which I never saw.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Well, you said it was propaganda, ma'am. That's what prompted me to ask --

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. This Muslim propaganda was very actual at -- in many times.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Very well. Mr. Alagic didn't share with you any of those thoughts?

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MARITA VIHERVUORI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And Mr. Alagic was not very -- not very, let's say, fundamentalistic, because we were drinking slivovitz with him.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARNAVAS
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Very well. Okay. We go on. I'm going to skip through some of this to save some time. If we go to the next page of -- of the transcript of the interview, and this would be on page 3 and I'm referring to 1D 01655. So we're back to your particular interview. We noticed, yesterday, there was some attention brought to this particular paragraph. It's the third paragraph on the top of the page, where it starts with Mr. Bartolomio visited Mostar, and it says here -- he goes on in the second sentence: "You know very well that the Croat side signed the document, the VO plan. We want to stop the war, and VO plan is probably the only solution of the existing Bosnia and Herzegovina. Without VO plan here are no Bosnia and Herzegovina. The war will last many years, and this fighting between Croats and Muslims is only in favour of Serbs or Chetniks." And then he goes on to say: "You know very well, tomorrow will be held council of two Serbian regions, Republika Srpska and Srpska Krajina." Do you know what Mr. Prlic is referring to at this point? It's on page -- it's on page 3 of the document with the number 1D 01655. That's the transcript of the tape.
